question: Why does the Moon affect water more than land?
answer: The Moon pulls on the whole Earth, but liquid particles can flow, so the sea piles up into a bulge. Solid ground is locked together and barely moves. That is why tides show up in the sea.
move: Water can flow, so it piles up under the Moon; rock can't.

web.label: Two side-by-side views of Earth under the Moon's pull: water bulging up toward the Moon, and solid ground that barely moves. Asks why the Moon affects water more than land.

source: Geopop, “Mont Saint-Michel: la magia delle maree di oltre 10 metri” (YouTube, 2018)
